name: Zen Center of Denver
technique: Shikantaza and koan-based zazen with dokusan/daisan teacher interviews
teacherAccess: Daily dokusan/daisan (private interviews) with fully transmitted teachers during sesshin and regular practice periods.
retreatOptions: Single-day zazenkai, and week-long sesshin (five to seven days), held on-site with optional overnight stay.
about: Founded in 1974, the Zen Center of Denver is an urban Zen Buddhist sangha rooted in the Harada-Yasutani lineage via Philip Kapleau and Robert Aitken, blending Soto and Rinzai traditions. Alongside daily zazen, dharma talks, and work practice, ZCD offers sesshin, week-long intensive silent retreats held one to two times per year at its own temple building. Participants can choose to stay overnight on-site (capacity around 20 beds), sleep at home, or join remotely via Zoom, with the same program and cost for all options. Sesshin includes formal oryoki-style vegetarian meals, work practice (samu), teacher interviews (dokusan/daisan), and teisho dharma talks. The center also runs a prison dharma program and community service work through the Zen Peacemakers network.
schedule: Weekly zazen and teisho year-round; monthly zazenkai (full-day sittings); sesshin (5-7 day silent retreats) offered about one to two times per year, usually summer and winter.
cost: Sesshin fees are calculated per day of the retreat, roughly $45/day for members and $55/day for non-members (e.g., ~$270 members / ~$330 non-members for a 6-day summer sesshin, including a non-refundable application fee); partial scholarships available for financial need.

pricePerDay.notes: Derived from ZCD's published per-day sesshin rate ($45/day members, $55/day non-members), applied identically whether staying on-site overnight, sleeping at home, or attending via Zoom.

foodNotes: Formal oryoki-style vegetarian meals served during sesshin and samu mornings.
workNotes: Sesshin includes periods of silent work practice (samu) as part of the schedule.
